record.paper_title: Ball-Evans approximation problem: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: Let f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω, R^n) be a homeomorphism whose Jacobian satisfies Jf ≡ 1 almost everywhere, so that f is incompressible. Can f be approximated in the Sobolev norm by a sequence of incompressible diffeomorphisms, or by piecewise affine incompressible homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Therefore in many modeling situations we actually work with incompressible deformations assuming that Jf ≡ 1 a.e.

Open problem 5. Ball-Evans mapping for incompressible homeomorphisms: Let f ∈ W1,p(Ω, R^n) be a homeomorphism with Jf ≡ 1 a.e. Can we find a sequence of incompressible diffeomorphisms (or piecewise affine incompressible homeomorphisms) which approximate f in the Sobolev norm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain ($n \geq 2$), and let $1 \leq p < \infty$. A mapping $f \in W^{1,p}(\Omega, \mathbb{R}^n)$ is called incompressible if it is a homeomorphism of $\Omega$ onto $f(\Omega)$ and its Jacobian determinant satisfies $J_f(x) := \det Df(x) = 1$ for almost every $x \in \Omega$.

Question: Given any incompressible homeomorphism $f \in W^{1,p}(\Omega, \mathbb{R}^n)$, does there exist a sequence $\{f_k\}$ of mappings such that $f_k \to f$ in the Sobolev norm $W^{1,p}(\Omega, \mathbb{R}^n)$, where each $f_k$ is either
(a) an incompressible diffeomorphism (i.e., a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism with $J_{f_k} \equiv 1$), or
(b) a piecewise affine incompressible homeomorphism (a homeomorphism that is affine on each simplex of some triangulation of $\Omega$, with $J_{f_k} = 1$ a.e.)?

Determine whether such an approximation is always possible, in any dimension $n \geq 2$ and for all admissible exponents $p$.
artifact.status_search_result: The incompressible Ball–Evans approximation problem is listed as an open problem in the recent survey on the Ball–Evans approximation problem. Even the unconstrained Ball–Evans problem (without the Jacobian = 1 constraint) is solved only in dimension 2 (Iwaniec–Kovalev–Onninen for 1<p<∞; Hencl–Pratelli for p=1), and remains open in higher dimensions. The incompressible variant adds the volume-preserving constraint and is not known in any dimension.

Can we find a sequence of incompressible diffeomorphisms (or piecewise affine incompressible homeomorphisms) which approximate f in the Sobolev norm?
status_evidence.claim: Listed explicitly as an open problem in a 2025 survey on the Ball–Evans approximation problem.

status_evidence.title: Approximation of W^{1,p} Sobolev homeomorphism by diffeomorphisms and the signs of the Jacobian
status_evidence.snippet: To date, there are no known results allowing approximation of Sobolev homeomorphisms by diffeomorphisms in the Sobolev space in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The unconstrained higher-dimensional Ball–Evans problem is itself open, supporting that the incompressible variant is open.
